text.p: Miami, notorious for its crooks and killers in recent years, is now less crime-plagued than its traditionally gentler neighbour Fort Lauderdale, a Miami Herald analysis said on Monday.

Once the U.S. big-city crime leader as tourists were murdered, prostitutes dismembered and gunfire exchanged in the streets by cocaine gangs, Miami dropped to sixth place on the national crime list in 1996, according to new FBI statistics.

Miami has been first twice this decade and was third in 1995. But Fort Lauderdale, a former mecca for college kids on spring break, is Florida's new crime capital. Fifth on the list in 1995, it climbed to second nationwide behind Atlanta and ahead of St. Louis, Baton Rouge and Tampa last year.
In violent crime, Miami placed fifth in the nation last year, down from third in 1995. Fort Lauderdale ranked 38th in violent crime but second in property crime.
Florida placed four cities in the top ten with Orlando ranked seventh.

Local officials, concerned about Miami's image, have long disputed the value of FBI statistics because they track the number of crimes per 1,000 residents while Miami has thousands of illegal immigrants, temporary residents and tourists who are not counted.
"The real success is when real people, the citizens, say they feel safer," Police Chief Donald Warshaw told the Herald. "I won't be happy until we're not even in the top 100."
